categories.name: validation
why: P2 because it restructures block admission, storage, and activation to allow concurrent validation
Author's benchmark shows a 5% IBD time cut and up to 98% lower tail latency for peer messaging
Lays groundwork for future parallel validation of sibling blocks, but carries real correctness risk needing careful review

categories.name: p2p
why: P2 because it removes a known contention hazard that stalls responses to all other peers during block validation
Benefits every peer connected during block processing, not just the one whose block is being validated
Addresses a pain point flagged since earlier related PRs, improving liveness under load

why: P3 because it changes shutdown/interrupt ordering that other subsystems depend on
